mainTopic: The seriousness of חנופה, and the opening of פרק משוח מלחמה: the war-priest's speech and who gives it
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that ירמיהו was punished for flattering חנניה: חנניה's grandson is the one who arrested him. רבי אלעזר then teaches, from the word גלמוד, that a group with חנופה is repulsive like a נדה and will end up in exile. רבי ירמיה בר אבא lists four groups who will not greet the שכינה: scoffers, flatterers, liars, and those who speak לשון הרע. Each one is proven from a פסוק. Then פרק אלו נאמרין ends, and a new פרק opens with a משנה about the כהן משוח מלחמה, who speaks to the army in לשון הקודש. The משנה explains his speech line by line: real enemies show no mercy, do not fear the noises of battle, and ה׳ fights for you through the ארון. The גמרא explains the לשון הקודש rule with a גזירה שוה from מתן תורה. It then shows that the speaking כהן must be appointed and have a superior in his own job, which rules out the כהן גדול and the סגן. Finally, it explains 'שמע ישראל' as a hint to the merit of קריאת שמע, and begins a ברייתא saying the כהן speaks twice, at the border and at the battle.

steps.title: חנניה's grandson arrests ירמיהו
steps.stepSummary: Verses from ירמיהו show that the officer who seized ירמיהו was יראייה, the grandson of חנניה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verses say that when ירמיהו was at the Benjamin Gate, a guard officer named יראייה son of שלמיה son of חנניה grabbed him and accused him of running away to the Babylonians. ירמיהו said this was false. Then the verse says יראייה grabbed ירמיהו and brought him to the officers.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a point that started on the previous amud. It quotes verses showing that ירמיהו was arrested by a grandson of חנניה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The key detail is the officer's family line: 'son of שלמיה son of חנניה.' The idea is measure for measure. ירמיהו flattered חנניה, so he was punished by falling into the hands of חנניה's grandson.

keyTerms.meaning: An officer of the guard; a captain in charge of a post
Here it means defecting or running over to the enemy, not physically falling

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'אתה נופל' as 'you are falling down.' In this verse it means 'you are deserting to the enemy.'

phrases.english: "And when he was at the Benjamin Gate,
there was an officer of the guard there,

phrases.aramaic: וּשְׁמוֹ יִרְאִיָּה בֶּן שֶׁלֶמְיָה בֶּן חֲנַנְיָה
phrases.english: whose name was Irijah son of Shelemiah son of Hananiah;
and he seized Jeremiah the prophet, saying:
You are defecting to the Chaldeans.
And Jeremiah said to him:

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁקֶר אֵינֶנִּי נֹפֵל אֶל הַכַּשְׂדִּים וְגוֹ׳״,
phrases.english: It is false; I am not defecting to the Chaldeans, etc."
And it is written: "And he seized Jeremiah
and brought him to the officers."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the proof begun before this section, that ירמיהו was punished for flattering חנניה.
steps.raayaObject: That ירמיהו was punished measure for measure for flattering חנניה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ירמיהו 37:13–14, which names the officer who arrested ירמיהו as חנניה's grandson.

steps.title: A flattering group is as repulsive as a נדה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that any group with חנופה in it is disgusting, like a נדה. He learns this from the word גלמוד in a verse in איוב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Any group that has flattery in it is disgusting, like a נדה. The verse says, 'For a flattering group is גלמוד,' and in the coastal cities people call a נדה 'גלמודה.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a new teaching about how bad flattery is. He compares a flattering group to a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The verse in איוב calls a flattering group 'גלמוד.' רבי אלעזר points out that in the coastal cities the word 'גלמודה' is used for a נדה. So the verse is really calling a flattering group repulsive, like a נדה.

keyTerms.meaning: Flattery; praising or going along with wrongdoers to please them
A woman in her menstrual state, who is separated from her husband
The coastal cities, or cities overseas

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any congregation that has flattery in it
is repulsive like a niddah,
as it is said: "For a flattering congregation is galmud,"
for in the coastal cities
they call a niddah 'galmuda.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the story of ירמיהו to general teachings about flattery.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group that tolerates חנופה is as repulsive as a נדה, based on the word גלמוד.

steps.title: What the word גלמודה means
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why a נדה is called גלמודה: she is separated from her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'גלמודה' mean? It means 'separated from her husband.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to explain the word גלמודה, so we understand why it fits a נדה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word גלמודה is read as two words joined together: גמולה (separated or weaned) and מבעלה (from her husband). A נדה is forbidden to her husband during this time. That is why the word fits her.

keyTerms.meaning: Lonely or desolate; here explained as 'separated from her husband'
Separated or cut off, like a baby weaned from nursing

phrases.english: What is 'galmuda'?
Separated from her husband.
phrases.notes: A wordplay: the גמרא reads גַּלְמוּדָה as גְּמוּלָה (separated) plus מִבַּעְלָהּ (from her husband).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the key word used in רבי אלעזר's teaching.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word גלמודה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means גמולה מבעלה, separated from her husband.

steps.title: A flattering group will end up in exile
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that a group with חנופה will eventually be exiled. He links the word גלמוד in איוב to the same word in ישעיהו, where it appears next to 'גולה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Any group that has flattery in it will in the end go into exile. Here it says, 'For a flattering group is גלמוד.' And there it says, 'You will say in your heart: Who gave birth to these for me, when I was bereaved and lonely (גלמודה), exiled and wandering?'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives a second teaching about flattery. This time the punishment is exile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He uses the same word, גלמוד, but compares it to another verse. In ישעיהו, 'גלמודה' appears right next to 'גולה' (exiled). So 'גלמוד' in איוב must also point to exile.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is written here... and it is written there': a way of linking two verses through a shared word

steps.whatToRemember: The single word גלמוד teaches two things about a flattering group: it is repulsive like a נדה, and it will end up in exile.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Any congregation that has flattery in it
will in the end go into exile.
It is written here: "For a flattering congregation is galmud,"
and it is written there:
"Then you will say in your heart:
Who has given birth to these for me,
when I was bereaved and galmuda,
exiled and wandering, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:21. Since 'exiled' sits right next to גלמודה, the two words go together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching from the same verse in איוב, now linked to a verse in ישעיהו.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A group that tolerates חנופה will ultimately be exiled.

steps.title: Four groups who will not greet the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה בר אבא lists four groups who will not greet the שכינה: scoffers, flatterers, liars, and people who speak לשון הרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא said: Four groups will not greet the שכינה. They are the group of scoffers, the group of flatterers, the group of liars, and the group of people who speak לשון הרע.
steps.whatsHappening: A new אמורא adds another teaching. He puts flatterers on a list of four groups who are kept away from the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The list itself is the whole statement here. Flatterers are placed alongside scoffers, liars, and people who speak לשון הרע. This shows how serious the sin of flattery is.

keyTerms.meaning: Greet, or receive, the Divine Presence
Evil speech; saying negative things about others

steps.whyThisMatters: This statement shows that flattery is not a minor social flaw. It belongs in the same category as lying and לשון הרע.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba said:
Four groups
will not greet the Divine Presence:
the group of scoffers, and the group of flatterers,
and the group of liars,
and the group of those who speak lashon hara.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the theme of how serious flattery is, now with a list of four groups.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Scoffers, flatterers, liars, and speakers of לשון הרע will not greet the שכינה.

steps.title: Verses for scoffers, flatterers, and liars
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק for each of the first three groups, showing that each is kept away from ה׳'s presence.
steps.simpleTranslation: The group of scoffers: as it says, 'He drew His hand away from scoffers.' The group of flatterers: as it says, 'A flatterer shall not come before Him.' The group of liars: as it says, 'One who speaks lies shall not stand before My eyes.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is now proving רבי ירמיה בר אבא's list from step 5. It brings one פסוק for each of the first three groups.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק describes ה׳ pushing a certain kind of person away from Him. ה׳ draws His hand away from scoffers, flatterers cannot come before Him, and liars cannot stand before His eyes. This shows that these groups will not greet the שכינה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is written. This introduces a פסוק used as a proof.
Scoffers, people who mock serious things.
Will not be established, will not stand.

phrases.english: The group of scoffers, as it is written:
"He drew His hand away from scoffers."
The group of flatterers, as it is written:
"For a flatterer shall not come before Him."
The group of liars, as it is written:
"One who speaks lies shall not stand before My eyes."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the first three groups listed in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: רבי ירמיה בר אבא's claim that scoffers, flatterers, and liars will not greet the שכינה.

steps.title: Verse for people who speak לשון הרע
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the fourth group from a פסוק in תהלים and explains it: evil will not dwell where ה׳ dwells.
steps.simpleTranslation: The group of people who speak לשון הרע: as it says, 'For You are not a God who desires wickedness; evil shall not dwell with You.' This means: You, ה׳, are righteous, so evil will not live in Your dwelling place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the last proof, for people who speak לשון הרע. It then explains the פסוק in its own words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'לא יגורך רע' are read as 'evil will not live in Your home.' Since ה׳ is righteous, evil people cannot be where He is. The פסוק itself only says 'רע', and the גמרא does not spell out here why this means לשון הרע specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: People who tell לשון הרע, harmful talk about others.

steps.whatToRemember: All four groups — scoffers, flatterers, liars, and people who speak לשון הרע — have a פסוק showing that ה׳ keeps them away from His presence.

phrases.english: The group of those who speak לשון הרע, as it is written:
"For You are not a God who desires wickedness;
evil shall not dwell with You."
You, ה׳, are righteous;
evil shall not dwell in Your dwelling place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of proofs begun in step 6 with the fourth group.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that people who speak לשון הרע will not greet the שכינה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: תהלים 5:5, read as: evil will not dwell in ה׳'s dwelling place.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אלו נאמרין
steps.stepSummary: The פרק אלו נאמרין ends with the traditional closing line.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אלו נאמרין.
steps.whatsHappening: This line is not part of the discussion. It marks the end of the פרק אלו נאמרין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We say 'הדרן עלך' at the end of every פרק to show we plan to come back and learn it again. The next line begins a new פרק.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you. This is the closing line said at the end of a perek.
'These are said'. This is the name of the perek that just ended.

phrases.english: We will return to you, "These Are Said."
phrases.notes: This is the name of the perek that just ended, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Formally closes the perek after the last aggadic teaching.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: פרק אלו נאמרין is finished, and a new פרק begins.

steps.title: The war-priest speaks to the army in Hebrew
steps.stepSummary: The new פרק's משנה teaches that the כהן משוח מלחמה addressed the soldiers in לשון הקודש, and brings a פסוק from דברים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The priest anointed for war, when he speaks to the people, would speak in the holy language (Hebrew). As it says: 'And it shall be, when you approach the battle, the priest shall come forward.' This is the priest anointed for war. 'And he shall speak to the people' means in the holy language.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק opens with a משנה about the special כהן who spoke to the Jewish army before battle. The משנה rules that he spoke in Hebrew.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה reads the פסוק in two parts. 'The priest' refers to a specific priest, the כהן משוח מלחמה. 'And he shall speak' teaches that he must speak in לשון הקודש. The משנה does not explain how the word 'speak' shows Hebrew; the גמרא asks about this in step 15 and answers it in step 16.

keyTerms.meaning: The priest anointed for war, who speaks to the army before battle.
As it is said. This introduces a פסוק.
And he shall come forward or approach.

steps.whyThisMatters: This משנה is the starting point for the whole new פרק, which deals with the war-priest's speech and the laws of going out to war.

phrases.english: The priest anointed for war,
phrases.notes: These words are also the name of the new perek.

phrases.english: at the time that he speaks to the people,
would speak in the holy language,
as it is said:
"And it shall be, when you approach the battle,
the priest shall come forward" —
this is the priest anointed for war;
"and he shall speak to the people" —
in the holy language.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְשׁוּחַ מִלְחָמָה בְּשָׁעָה שֶׁמְּדַבֵּר אֶל הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new perek and a completely new topic after the הדרן.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן משוח מלחמה must address the army in לשון הקודש, learned from 'ונגש הכהן ודבר אל העם'.

steps.title: Against your enemies, not against your brothers
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the words 'על אויביכם': this war is against enemies, not against fellow tribes who would have pity on you.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן says to them, 'Hear, Israel, you are going against your enemies.' This means: not against your brothers. Not יהודה against שמעון, and not שמעון against בנימין. If you fell into a brother's hands, he would have mercy on you.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה keeps explaining the כהן's speech word by word. Here it focuses on the words 'against your enemies.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is a warning. In a war between tribes, a captured soldier could expect kindness. This war is against real enemies, so the soldiers must take it seriously.

keyTerms.meaning: Hear, Israel. The opening words of the כהן's speech

phrases.english: "And he shall say to them: Hear, Israel
etc., against your enemies"
and not against your brothers,
not Yehuda against Shimon
and not Shimon against Binyamin.
For if you fall into their hands
they will have mercy on you,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר אֲלֵיהֶם שְׁמַע יִשְׂרָאֵל וְגוֹ׳ עַל אוֹיְבֵיכֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's reading of the כהן's speech that began in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words 'against your enemies' mean this is a war against real enemies, not a war between Jewish tribes, where captives would be treated kindly.

steps.title: Proof that brothers show mercy, so enemies will not
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a פסוק showing how Jewish captors once cared for their Jewish captives, then contrasts this with real enemies, who show no mercy.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the פסוק says: the men who were named got up and took the captives. They dressed everyone who was naked, gave them shoes, fed them, gave them drink, and anointed them with oil. They carried the weak ones on donkeys and brought them to יריחו, near their brothers, and returned to שומרון. But you are going against enemies. If you fall into their hands, they will not have mercy on you.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה proves that brothers have mercy, using a story where captors took gentle care of Jewish captives. Then it makes the contrast: enemies will not do this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes soldiers of שומרון, the northern kingdom, caring for captives they had taken from יהודה. That shows how a war between brothers ends with kindness. Real enemies will not act this way, so the soldiers must be ready.

keyTerms.meaning: Shomron, the capital of the northern kingdom

phrases.english: as it is stated:
"And the men who were named rose up
phrases.notes: דברי הימים ב 28:15. These were men of Shomron returning captives they had taken from יהודה.

phrases.english: and took the captives,
and with the spoil they clothed all who were naked among them;
they dressed them and gave them shoes,
fed them, gave them drink, and anointed them,
and carried all the weak ones on donkeys,
and brought them to Yericho, the city of palm trees,
near their brothers, and they returned to Shomron, etc."
But you are going against your enemies;

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם תִּפְּלוּ בְּיָדָם אֵין מְרַחֲמִין עֲלֵיכֶם.
phrases.english: if you fall into their hands, they will not have mercy on you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proves the claim from step 10 that brothers show mercy, then states the contrast with enemies.
steps.raayaObject: That fellow Jews who capture you will have mercy on you.
steps.raayaSupportSource: דברי הימים ב 28:15, where the men of Shomron cared for the captives from יהודה and returned them.

steps.title: Four kinds of battle-fear
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains each of the four fear-words in the פסוק as a different frightening sound of battle.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Do not let your heart be faint, do not fear, do not panic.' Do not let your heart be faint because of horses neighing and swords being sharpened. Do not fear because of shields banging and boots stomping. Do not panic at the sound of trumpets. Do not be terrified by the sound of shouting.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה takes four phrases that all sound like 'don't be scared' and gives each one its own meaning: a different noise of war.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to repeat itself, so the משנה reads each phrase as a separate fear. Each one matches a sound the enemy makes to frighten soldiers: animals, weapons, armor, trumpets, and battle cries.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not let your heart be faint

phrases.english: "Let not your heart be faint; do not fear,
and do not panic, etc."
"Let not your heart be faint":
because of the neighing of horses
and the sharpening of swords;
"Do not fear":
because of the banging of shields
and the noise of boots;
phrases.notes: קַלְגַּסִּין are soldiers' heavy boots, stomping loudly as the army marches.

phrases.english: "Do not panic": at the sound of trumpets;
"Do not be terrified": because of the sound of shouting.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַל יֵרַךְ לְבַבְכֶם אַל תִּירְאוּ וְאַל תַּחְפְּזוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next part of the same פסוק in the כהן's speech.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each of the four fear-expressions refers to a different frightening sound of battle.

steps.title: ה׳ goes with you
steps.stepSummary: The משנה explains the reason not to be afraid: the enemy relies on a human hero, while Israel relies on ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For ה׳ your God is the One who goes with you.' They come trusting in the victory of a human being, and you come trusting in the victory of ה׳.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה reaches the next פסוק, which gives the reason to be brave. It sets up a contrast that the next step will illustrate with examples.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The enemy's confidence rests on a human champion, who can be beaten. Israel's confidence rests on ה׳, who cannot be beaten.

keyTerms.meaning: His victory, meaning the strength of a champion
Flesh and blood, a human being

phrases.english: "For ה׳ your God is the One who goes with you."

phrases.aramaic: הֵם בָּאִין בְּנִצְחוֹנוֹ שֶׁל בָּשָׂר וָדָם,
phrases.english: They come trusting in the victory of flesh and blood,
and you come trusting in the victory of ה׳.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind the command in step 12 not to be afraid.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The enemy trusts in a human hero, but Israel goes out with ה׳.

steps.title: גלית and שובך fell, and their armies with them
steps.stepSummary: The משנה shows from history that armies trusting in a human hero fell when he fell. Then it says Israel is different, because ה׳ goes with them in the camp of the ארון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פלשתים came trusting in גלית. What happened to him in the end? He fell by the sword, and they fell with him. עמון came trusting in שובך. What happened to him in the end? He fell by the sword, and they fell with him. But you are not like that: 'For ה׳ your God goes with you, to fight for you.' This refers to the camp of the ארון.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives two examples from תנ״ך to prove that trusting in a human hero fails. Then it explains what 'ה׳ goes with you' means in practice: the ארון goes out with the army.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both examples follow the same pattern: when the hero dies, his whole army falls with him. Israel's 'hero' is ה׳, who does not fall. The last line connects the פסוק to something physical, the camp that carried the ארון to war.

keyTerms.meaning: גלית, the champion of the פלשתים
שובך, the commander of the army of הדדעזר, which fought on the side of עמון
The camp that carried the ארון into battle

steps.whatToRemember: The speech has three messages: these are real enemies who show no mercy, don't give in to the frightening sounds of war, and ה׳, who is present through the ארון, fights for you.

phrases.english: The Philistines came trusting in the victory of Goliath.
What was his end?
In the end he fell by the sword, and they fell with him.

phrases.aramaic: בְּנֵי עַמּוֹן בָּאוּ בְּנִצְחוֹנוֹ שֶׁל שׁוֹבַךְ,
phrases.english: The people of Amon came trusting in the victory of Shovach.
What was his end?
In the end he fell by the sword, and they fell with him.
But you, you are not like that:
"For ה׳ your God goes with you
to fight for you, etc."
This is the camp of the Ark.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses examples from history to illustrate the contrast stated in step 13, and closes the משנה's reading of the speech.
steps.raayaObject: That an army trusting in a human hero falls when the hero falls.
steps.raayaSupportSource: גלית and the פלשתים, and שובך and עמון, who each fell together with their armies.

steps.title: What does the משנה mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking how the משנה's פסוק shows that the speech must be in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the משנה saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the start of the משנה (step 9), which said the כהן speaks in לשון הקודש and quoted a פסוק. It asks what proof that פסוק gives, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק the משנה quoted only says the כהן 'shall speak.' It says nothing about which language. So the גמרא wants to know how the משנה learned that it means לשון הקודש.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for גמרא; the discussion of the משנה begins here
What is it saying? A request to explain unclear wording

steps.confusionAlert: This question is not about the speech we just read (steps 10-14). It goes back to the opening line of the משנה about לשון הקודש.

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is it saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא and returns to the משנה's opening claim from step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How does the פסוק quoted in the משנה prove that the כהן speaks in לשון הקודש?

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה uses a גזירה שוה. The word 'speak' is used here and also at מתן תורה, where the speech was in לשון הקודש.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means. The פסוק here says 'and he shall speak.' Elsewhere, at מתן תורה, it says 'משה would speak, and God would answer him with a voice.' Just as there the speech was in לשון הקודש, so too here it is in לשון הקודש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question. The proof comes from linking the same word, 'speak,' in two places.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both פסוקים use the root דבר, 'speak.' At מתן תורה the speaking was clearly in לשון הקודש. Through the shared word, that same rule carries over to the כהן's speech.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means. Introduces an explanation
There, meaning in a different פסוק

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a short proof in a משנה can depend on a hidden גזירה שוה, and the גמרא spells it out.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
since it is stated "and he shall speak,"
phrases.notes: דברים 20:2, about the כהן speaking to the army.

phrases.english: and elsewhere it says:
"Moshe would speak, and God would answer him with a voice,"
just as there it was in the holy tongue,
so too here it is in the holy tongue.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה on the word 'speak' links the כהן's speech to מתן תורה, which was in לשון הקודש.

steps.title: The speaking priest must be an appointed official
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא compares the כהן to the שוטרים. Just as the officers are appointed officials, the כהן who speaks must also be an appointed official.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: 'And the priest shall approach and speak to the people.' You might think any priest who wants to can speak. So the פסוק says, 'And the officers shall speak.' Just as the officers are appointed officials, so too the priest must be an appointed official.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that tells us which כהן gives the speech to the army. He must be an appointed official, not just any כהן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא links two פסוקים in the same section that both use the word 'speak'. One is about the כהן and one is about the שוטרים. Since the שוטרים are clearly appointed officials, the כהן must be one too.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this opens a ברייתא

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
"And the priest shall approach and speak to the people."
I might think any priest who wishes may speak.
So the verse teaches: "And the officers shall speak."
Just as the officers are appointed officials,
so too the priest must be an appointed official.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: וְנִגַּשׁ הַכֹּהֵן וְדִבֶּר אֶל הָעָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the language of the speech to the identity of the speaker.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן who addresses the army must be an appointed official, like the שוטרים.

steps.title: Maybe it should be the כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the speaker should not be the כהן גדול, who is the most appointed כהן of all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it is the כהן גדול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. If the speaker must be an appointed כהן, why not the כהן גדול?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If being 'appointed' is all that is needed, the כהן גדול would be the obvious choice. The ברייתא never said that, so the גמרא asks what rules him out.

phrases.english: But say it is the High Priest?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the word 'appointed' reaches in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's rule that the speaker is an appointed כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כהן גדול is the highest appointed כהן, so he should qualify.

steps.title: Like an officer, he must have someone above him
steps.stepSummary: The comparison to the שוטר goes further. A שוטר has a superior over him, so the כהן must also have a superior over him.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like an officer. Just as an officer has an appointed official above him, so too the priest must have an appointed official above him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the comparison to the officers teaches a second detail. The speaking כהן must be someone who has a boss above him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The comparison now covers two things. The speaker must be appointed, and he must also have someone appointed over him. That seems to rule out the כהן גדול, who is at the top.

phrases.english: It is similar to an officer:

phrases.aramaic: מָה שׁוֹטֵר שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְמוּנֶּה עַל גַּבָּיו —
phrases.english: just as an officer has an appointed official above him,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כֹּהֵן שֶׁיֵּשׁ מְמוּנֶּה עַל גַּבָּיו.
phrases.english: so too the priest must be one who has an appointed official above him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 18 by adding a second point to the comparison.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Expands the comparison to add a requirement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any appointed כהן qualifies, even the כהן גדול.
steps.terutzMaskana: The speaker must be an appointed כהן who has a superior above him.

steps.title: The כהן גדול also has the מלך above him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. The כהן גדול also has someone above him, namely the מלך.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן גדול also has someone above him, since there is the מלך!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the last answer. Even the כהן גדול has a superior, because the מלך is above him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule is simply 'someone is above him', the כהן גדול still passes, because the מלך outranks him. So the new requirement does not rule him out yet.

phrases.english: The High Priest also,
there is the king above him!

steps.triggerLanguage: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל נָמֵי, הָאִיכָּא מֶלֶךְ עַל גַּבָּיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: The requirement of having someone above him
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The מלך is above the כהן גדול, so the כהן גדול meets the requirement.

steps.title: Someone above him in his own job
steps.stepSummary: The superior must be above him in his own role, the עבודה. The מלך is not above the כהן גדול in the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is speaking about someone above him in his service.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'someone above him' means someone above him in his own work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מלך is the boss of the country, not the boss of the כהנים in the עבודה. In the עבודה no one is above the כהן גדול, so he is ruled out.

keyTerms.meaning: The service in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: It is speaking about someone above him in his service.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20 by narrowing the meaning of 'above him'.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any superior at all counts, even the מלך.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a superior in his own job counts, so the כהן גדול is ruled out.

steps.title: Maybe it should be the סגן
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the סגן, who has the כהן גדול above him in the עבודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then say it is the סגן!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries another candidate, the סגן, who seems to fit both requirements perfectly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סגן is a high official, and the כהן גדול is above him in the עבודה. So the question is why the ברייתא does not name him as the speaker.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy of the כהן גדול

phrases.english: Then say it is the deputy!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new candidate who seems to fit the refined rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: The unnamed identity of the speaking כהן
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סגן is appointed and has a superior in the עבודה, so he should be the speaker.

steps.title: The deputy is not a true appointed office
steps.stepSummary: The סגן does not count as a ממונה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The deputy is not an appointed official.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the סגן fails the first requirement, because he is not really an appointed official.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סגן has a superior, but his position is not a true appointed office. So he fails the basic requirement taught in the ברייתא.

phrases.english: The deputy is not an appointed official.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies that the candidate fits the category
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סגן is an appointed official with a superior.
steps.terutzMaskana: The סגן is not a true ממונה, so he cannot be the speaker.

steps.title: Proof: the deputy is only a backup
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים says the סגן exists only to replace the כהן גדול if the כהן גדול becomes unfit.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים said: Why is a סגן appointed? So that if the כהן גדול becomes unfit, the סגן can step in and serve in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that the סגן is not a true appointed office. His only role is to stand ready as a backup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a man who held the job of סגן admits that it has no work of its own. It exists only as a replacement, so it does not count as a ממונה. This finishes the search for the speaker, who must be a different appointed כהן.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

steps.whatToRemember: The כהן who speaks to the army must be appointed and must have a superior in his own job. That rules out the כהן גדול, who has no one above him in the עבודה. It also rules out the סגן, who is only a backup and not a real appointed office.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
Rabbi Ḥanina, the deputy of the priests, said:
Why is a deputy appointed?

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁאִם אֵירַע בּוֹ פְּסוּל בְּכֹהֵן גָּדוֹל,
phrases.english: So that if a disqualification happens to the High Priest,
he enters and serves in his place.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא סְגַן הַכֹּהֲנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the claim in step 23.
steps.raayaObject: That the סגן is not a true appointed office
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חנינא סגן הכהנים

steps.title: Why the speech opens with 'Hear Israel'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the כהן's speech uses the words 'שמע ישראל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he shall say to them: Hear Israel.' What is special about the words 'Hear Israel'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next words of the speech. It asks why the כהן opens with 'שמע ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wording seems chosen on purpose. The גמרא wants to know what message these exact words carry for soldiers going to war.

phrases.english: "And he shall say to them: Hear Israel."
What is different that it says "Hear Israel"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the wording of the speech.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the speech opens with the words 'שמע ישראל'

steps.title: Even the merit of saying שמע protects them
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן, quoting רבי שמעון בן יוחי, says that 'שמע ישראל' hints that the merit of קריאת שמע alone keeps Israel from falling to the enemy.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחי: הקדוש ברוך הוא said to ישראל: Even if you kept nothing except reciting שמע morning and evening, you will not be handed over into their hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the words 'שמע ישראל' remind the soldiers of קריאת שמע. That merit alone is enough to protect them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase links the war speech to the daily קריאת שמע. The message is that even a small, steady מצוה done every morning and evening protects Israel from its enemies.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows how much weight חז״ל give to the daily מצוה of קריאת שמע. It is enough to protect the nation in war.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לָהֶן הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא לְיִשְׂרָאֵל:
phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said to Israel:
Even if you have fulfilled nothing
except reciting Shema morning and evening,
you will not be handed over into their hands.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'שמע ישראל' hints that the merit of קריאת שמע alone protects Israel in battle.

steps.title: The priest speaks twice: at the border and at the battle
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא on 'אל ירך לבבכם' teaches that the כהן speaks to the army twice, at the border and on the battlefield. It then begins to say what he says at the border.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Let not your heart faint; do not fear,' and so on. The Rabbis taught: He speaks with them twice, once at the border and once at the battle. At the border, what does he say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא saying that the כהן gives two speeches. It is setting up the next part, which will tell us what he says at the border.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now the speech sounded like one event. This ברייתא splits it into two moments: when the army gathers at the border, and when it reaches the battlefield. The line ends with a question that is answered on the next amud.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't stop at the end of this line. 'At the border, what does he say?' is only an opening question, and its answer comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: "Let not your heart faint; do not fear," and so on.
The Rabbis taught:
He speaks with them twice:
once at the border, and once at the battle.
phrases.notes: 'The border' is where the army gathers before heading out to fight.

phrases.english: At the border, what does he say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next words of the speech and introduces a new ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן משוח מלחמה speaks to the army twice: once at the border and once on the battlefield.
